sections.title: Turning office hours into an agentic opportunity
sections.subtitle: My content team has had to evolve and roll with the AI-punches over the last few years. Here's exactly how I redefined an old, dusty way of working to meet the moment and achieve concrete results

sections.heading: Our focus shifted from UX, to "engineering", to Systems
sections.intro: The through-line: we designed (and maintained) the system that makes good UX writing repeatable.

items.title: From becoming "AI-first"...
items.description: UX writing all up gave way to UX for new agents and AI-first products.

items.title: ...to content engineering...
items.description: Evals, response quality, and building our own Content Design agent(s).

items.title: ...to building the system
items.description: A cross-org Language System, a DPG content repo, and a shared definition of Quality.

sections.heading: But that meant shifting how we work. We went from being embedded in vertical product spaces, to horizontal systems. Which brought back the bone-chilling specter of...
Office hours evolved
sections.caption: Office hours often start as a noble attempt to scale limited content design resources across a massive product org, but they frequently devolve. While the product team is (hopefully) left happy by the results, the content designer has very little to show for it
